provenance.original: TSA also calculates a time burden associated with the applicant’s travel to and from the healthcare provider’s office, as well as time spent at the appointment and time to print and submit forms to TSA.  TSA assumes applicants travel to their healthcare provider by private vehicle and that it takes approximately 20 minutes (0.33 hours) to reach the provider’s office, resulting in a 0.66 hour round-trip (0.33 hours x 2).  In addition, TSA estimates that, on average, applicants will incur an in-office wait time of 11 minutes (0.18 hours), and will spend 30 minutes waiting for the healthcare provider to complete the forms (0.5 hours).  TSA also assumes that it will take 5 minutes (0.08 hours) to print the forms and email them to TSA.  This results in a total time burden of 1.42 hours per applicant to travel to and from and attend the appointment and submit the forms (0.66 hours + 0.18 hours + 0.50 hours + 0.08 hours).  The travel time burden is recognized for applicants only, as incumbents’ travel time is considered to be within the scope of their duties as TSA employees.  The total public travel and wait time burden and associated cost are displayed in Table 3.

provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

provenance.original: Aircraft Operators covered under this program must submit information for all passengers to Secure Flight in the form of SFPD.  The vast majority of SFPD messages submitted by the Aircraft Operators are identified as a low or neutral risk by the Secure Fight automated engine.  Those records identified as requiring additional review are inhibited by the Secure Flight engine, and the passengers with inhibited boarding pass must go the Aircraft Operator ticket counter for additional assistance.  Aircraft Operators must submit additional information on inhibited passengers to TSA.  Generally, this information is gathered from the passenger’s VID and submitted electronically to TSA (a VID submission).  There are currently 222 Aircraft Operators covered by this collection; in addition, TSA expects 20 Aircraft Operators per year to be added each year.  TSA estimates an average of 990 annual VID submissions per covered Aircraft Operator, and 130 seconds (0.0361 hours) per response.  Certain submissions may require a Resolution Call to TSA to provide additional information.  TSA estimates that each carrier will be required to make an average of 230 calls per year.  TSA estimates a Resolution Call will require 12 minutes (0.2 hours).  The total annual hour burden for covered Aircraft Operators is 21,418.5 hours, or 64,256 hours over 3 years.  Table 1 summarizes these estimates.
